1-2: I give thanks before You, living and enduring King, for You have returned my soul to me with compassion; great is Your faithfulness.
2-2: Blessed are You, Lord our God, King of the universe, who has made us holy with His commandments and commanded us concerning the washing of the hands.
2-4: Blessed are You, Lord our God, King of the universe, who formed man in wisdom and created in him many openings and many hollows. It is revealed and known before Your throne of glory that if one of them were to be blocked, or if one of them were to be opened, it would be impossible to survive even for one hour. Blessed are You, Lord, who heals all flesh and acts wondrously.
2-6: My God, the soul You placed in me is pure. You created it, You formed it, You breathed it into me, You guard it within me, and one day You will take it from me and return it to me in the time to come. As long as the soul is within me, I give thanks before You, Lord my God and God of my fathers, Master of all works, Lord of all souls. Blessed are You, Lord, who returns souls to lifeless bodies.
2-7: Blessed are You, Lord our God, King of the universe, who gave the rooster understanding to tell day from night.
2-8: Blessed are You, Lord our God, King of the universe, who opens the eyes of the blind.
2-9: Blessed are You, Lord our God, King of the universe, who frees the bound.
2-10: Blessed are You, Lord our God, King of the universe, who straightens those who are bent.
2-11: Blessed are You, Lord our God, King of the universe, who clothes the naked.
2-12: Blessed are You, Lord our God, King of the universe, who gives strength to the weary.
2-13: Blessed are You, Lord our God, King of the universe, who spreads out the earth above the waters.
2-14: Blessed are You, Lord our God, King of the universe, who makes firm the steps of man.
2-16: Blessed are You, Lord our God, King of the universe, who has provided me with all I need.
2-17: Blessed are You, Lord our God, King of the universe, who girds Israel with might.
2-18: Blessed are You, Lord our God, King of the universe, who crowns Israel with glory.
2-19: Blessed are You, Lord our God, King of the universe, who has not made me a gentile.
2-20: Blessed are You, Lord our God, King of the universe, who has not made me a slave.
2-22: Blessed are You, Lord our God, King of the universe, who has not made me a woman.
2-24: Blessed is He who has made me according to His will.
2-25: Blessed are You, Lord our God, King of the universe, who removes the bonds of sleep from my eyes and slumber from my eyelids. May it be Your will, Lord my God and God of my fathers, to accustom me to Your Torah and make me cling to Your commandments. Do not bring me into sin, nor into wrongdoing, nor into temptation, nor into disgrace. Keep me far from the evil inclination and make me cling to the good inclination, and compel my inclination to serve You. Grant me today and every day grace, kindness and mercy in Your eyes and in the eyes of all who see me, and bestow good kindnesses upon me. Blessed are You, Lord, who bestows good kindnesses upon His people Israel.
2-26: May it be Your will, Lord my God and God of my fathers, to save me today and every day from the brazen and from brazenness, from a bad person, from the evil inclination, from a bad companion, from a bad neighbour, from a harmful mishap, from the evil eye and from evil speech, from a harsh judgement and from a harsh opponent in judgement, whether he is a member of the covenant or not.
3-1: Blessed are You, Lord our God, King of the universe, who has made us holy with His commandments and commanded us concerning the words of Torah.
3-2: Please make the words of Your Torah sweet, Lord our God, in our mouths and in the mouths of Your people, the house of Israel. May we, our children, our children's children and the children of Your people, the house of Israel, all know Your name and learn Your Torah for its own sake. Blessed are You, Lord, who teaches Torah to His people Israel.
3-3: Blessed are You, Lord our God, King of the universe, who chose us from all the nations and gave us His Torah. Blessed are You, Lord, who gives the Torah.
